episodes.202501: An area of low pressure moved along a slow moving cold front bringing numerous showers and thunderstorms to Virginia. Multiple rounds of heavy rain occurred throughout the afternoon and evening and into the overnight across portions of central Virginia. Total rainfall amounts of two to five inches were observed where flooding occurred.
episodes.202543: Another burst of abundant monsoon moisture resulted in localized heavy rainfall July 2nd and overnight into July 3rd. Burn scar flash flooding off the Salt burn scar washed out culverts that then diverted water into the Cherokee Mobile home park near Ruidoso. A late night round of strong thunderstorms developing along middle Rio Grande Valley produced very heavy rainfall measuring 1 to near 2.50 inches in Rio Rancho. Roads were washed out with dirt and debris in Rio Rancho and near Las Nutrias in northern Socorro County. Fast moving waters in the Albuquerque arroyo system swept away at least two people who were rescued, while a potential third person was reported also swept away.
episodes.202587: A broad trough of low pressure move through the northeast during the day kicking off a few sub severe storms in the morning then some scattered severe storms in the afternoon. These storms caused sporadic wind damage in MA and CT.
episodes.202621: Showers and thunderstorms moving across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska during the afternoon and evening hours produced gusty conditions and hail.
episodes.202666: A high-based thunderstorm moving across Washington County produced a 58 mph wind gust at the Akron Airport (Colorado Plains Regional Airport).
episodes.202779: Heavy rain from monsoon thunderstorms caused some flash flooding in Yavapai County.
episodes.202781: Deep tropical monsoon moisture interacted with an approaching upper level low moving towards the southern California coastline to bring strong thunderstorms and flash flooding to the region.
episodes.202827: A stalling cold front across central North Carolina and a prefrontal trough that developed across the Coastal Plain and tracked east towards the coast brought widespread shower and thunderstorm activity to much of Eastern North Carolina through the afternoon and evening on July second. Showers and thunderstorms developed across the Coastal Plain during the late morning hours, with this activity pushing east and merging into a large linear segment. A few storms became strong to severe within this line bringing strong wind gusts to the Roanoke, Croatan, and Pamlico Sounds as well as the waters around the Core Banks during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.202874: A cold front sagged down into the Ohio Valley region and eventually stalled out. This boundary was the focus for showers and thunderstorms to develop in a saturated environment, producing heavy rainfall, runoff, and flooding.
episodes.203244: An upper level trough brought embedded shortwaves aloft that developed thunderstorms in the region. Storms on July 1st were concentrated in Southwest MT. Coverage of thunderstorms became widespread across the region July 2nd due to better shear and moisture. The main hazards with storms were severe wind gusts.
episodes.203380: Slow moving thunderstorms produced isolated areas of flash flooding.
episodes.203738: An upper low pressure moved over the area and combined with an unstable airmass to produce two days of widespread showers and thunderstorms. The largest hail size was measured at 1 inch, but there were several reports of small hail accumulating up to 2 to 3 inches. Additionally, there were several reports of sub-severe thunderstorm wind gusts of 40-50 mph.
episodes.203739: An upper low pressure moved over the area and combined with an unstable airmass to produce two days of widespread showers and thunderstorms. The largest hail size was measured at 1 inch, but there were several reports of small hail accumulating up to 2 to 3 inches. Additionally, there were several reports of sub-severe thunderstorm wind gusts of 40-50 mph.
episodes.203750: A strong cold front produced widespread showers and thunderstorms. Some of these storms organized into lines and produced localized damaging wind gusts. A discrete supercell thunderstorm produced a brief tornado over southern Maryland.
episodes.203929: A partially cutoff low ejected through the region through early July, followed by a weaker trailing shortwave trough. This unsettled pattern resulted in sporadic instances of strong to severe wind gusts in addition to hail.
episodes.203941: The remnants of Tropical Storm Barry moved into our area, bringing plenty of moisture to the region. Multiple rounds of convection in this tropical airmass resulted in flash flooding across Reeves County in Texas, which prompted numerous road closures.
episodes.204263: Thunderstorms developed in the Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon hours of July 1st. As this activity tracked east into the eastern Nebraska Panhandle and northwestern Sandhills, it became severe. Hail up to 2 inches in diameter was reported in Sheridan County with the strongest storms.
episodes.204568: South to southeast flow at the surface combined with weak southerly flow aloft ahead of a west coast trough brought plenty of moisture into the Borderland with slow storm motion.  The heavy rain brought flash flooding to the recent Trout burn scar as well as along Highway 180 northwest of Deming.  An isolated severe thunderstorm brought wind damage to the Truth or Consequences area.
episodes.204669: A slow-moving cold front over the Ohio and Tennessee valley produced scattered to numerous showers and storms in the evening and early overnight hours. Most of the storms were sub-severe, but a few cells produced wind damage over the northwest Piedmont.
episodes.204670: A cold front stalled out over the western Piedmont of central North Carolina. Storms were ongoing during the morning and afternoon hours across central and eastern sections of the state. A stronger wave of afternoon and early evening storms moved across the Triangle, resulting in some isolated wind damage over Wake County.
episodes.205129: A trade wind perturbation resulted in an increased frequency of showers moving over eastern portions of Puerto Rico on July 2nd. Debris Flow was reported later in the afternoon at PR-183, close to the Pedro Rivera Molina Elementary School.
episodes.205197: A weak frontal boundary dropped across the Northland the 2nd into the 3rd. A few thunderstorms formed ahead of the front during the afternoon hours of the 2nd, but were mainly non-severe with limited instability in place. A few storms were a bit stronger and produced isolated wind damage in parts of Sawyer and Washburn counties.
episodes.205212: An upper-level trough and cold front progressed from the Great Lakes region into the Mid-Atlantic on July 1. Numerous thunderstorms, some of which produced swaths of damaging winds, developed ahead of the cold front in the late afternoon and evening hours across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.205237: Line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved south-southeastward across east central WI out over Lake Michigan producing damaging winds.
episodes.205263: An upper-level trough and cold front progressed from the Great Lakes region into the Mid-Atlantic on July 1. A line of thunderstorms moved across the Chesapeake Bay and onto the lower Maryland Eastern Shore in the evening hours, producing scattered damaging winds.
episodes.205264: An upper-level trough and cold front progressed from the Great Lakes region into the Mid-Atlantic on July 1. Numerous thunderstorms moved into central Virginia in the afternoon and evening hours. With training storms and very high rain rates, heavy rain led to nuisance flash flooding in some areas.
episodes.205303: During the early evening hours on July 2nd, a couple of strong to severe storms produced hail up to quarter sized and some minor tree damage in northeast Iowa.
episodes.205304: During the late afternoon and early evening hours on July 2nd, a few pop up thunderstorms produced strong downburst winds in southeast Minnesota which resulted in localized wind damage. A few instances of downed trees along with some structural damage were reported with these storms. Additionally, small hail up to dime sized was observed as well.
episodes.205529: Mid-morning developing convection within weak to moderate deep layer west to southwest flow over the state produces a funnel cloud near Pine Island in Lee County.
episodes.205531: Early afternoon convection within weak to moderate deep layer west to southwest flow over the state produces a waterspout offshore Sanibel Island in Lee County.
episodes.205566: Well above normal June rainfall over the White River basin, including almost 10 inches for the month near Bloomington, IN, along with heavy rain July 1st, resulted in river levels on the White River, briefly exceeding flood stage at Petersburg.
episodes.205688: Numerous severe downbursts developed from innocuous-looking mid level clouds, causing lots of damage in the Las Vegas Valley. No lightning was detected.
episodes.205779: A cold front tracked through the region and produced heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.205781: A stationary front was draped across the Mid-Atlantic early on July 2. In the afternoon, the front slowly advanced southward, serving as a focus for showers and storms through the day. Repeated training of showers and storms led to a significant flood event in rural southern Virginia in the late morning and early afternoon hours. In the late afternoon, a stationary shower produced localized, urban flash flooding in the city of Norfolk.
episodes.205782: A stationary front was draped across the Mid-Atlantic early on July 2. In the afternoon, the front slowly advanced southward, serving as a focus for showers and storms across northeast North Carolina through the day. Storms were slow-moving, had high rain rates, and trained over locations for an extended duration. This led to scattered instances of flash flooding.
episodes.205787: Several reports of severe weather events were received on the first day of the month.
episodes.205837: A stationary front was draped across the Mid-Atlantic early on July 2. In the afternoon, the front slowly advanced southward, serving as a focus for showers and storms across northeast North Carolina through the day. A storm briefly turned severe as it was moving through Currituck County, producing isolated wind damage.
episodes.205885: Scattered storms produced an isolated strong wind gust during the early morning hours 4 miles north northwest of the town of Crandall.
episodes.205937: Several severe thunderstorms developed over the Black Hills and produced large hail. The storms intensified as they moved east and produced some damaging wind gusts and hail up to 1.75.
episodes.206018: Low pressure passing through helped trigger thunderstorms over southern Nevada. A few produced high winds.
episodes.206022: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved northward through Southeastern Arizona the afternoon and evening of July 2nd, 2025. These storms caused severe wind gusts and thunderstorm wind damage causing power outages due to downed power lines and damage to equipment. Additionally, there was heavy rainfall causing flash flooding of roughly 3 feet of water moving through a low water crossing.
episodes.206188: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the northern Gulf waters on July 2, 2025, as a weak front lingered near the central Gulf Coast. A Weatherflow Tempest station measured a 39 mph (34 kt) wind gust in the coastal waters between Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River and Port Fourchon, Louisiana.
episodes.206318: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts near Cape Canaveral.
episodes.207944: A slow-moving cold front draped across northeast Lower and central Michigan provided enough lift for development of some stronger storms, particularly for Gladwin County, where some wind damage occurred. Additional reports of rotation and a wall cloud in the vicinity of Skidway Lake in southern Ogemaw county, but no damage was reported.
